findings.explanation: The SPL emits one row per 7040 or 7042 event with no repeat count. The detailedImplementation also says to trigger "when results are present", so a single 7040 notifies. The "repeated 7040" threshold in the implementation is never implemented or quantified.
findings.quote: notify the endpoint owner on any 7042 or repeated 7040.
findings.suggested_fix: Either state that every 7040 and 7042 row triggers, with repeated-7040 aggregation done only on the dashboard, or define the repeat threshold (N events per endpoint per period). Note that it requires a separate aggregating search.

findings.explanation: The linked Microsoft Q&A page is an anonymous user's forum question quoting their own event log, not Microsoft Support documentation. It is useful as a message-text example but not as vendor authority.
findings.quote: "title": "Microsoft Support example: Search Event IDs 7040 and 7042 catalog-corruption messages"
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle as "Microsoft Q&A community post: example Windows Search 7040/7042 event text", and do not treat it as normative.

findings.explanation: Microsoft's procedure deletes `.BLF`/`.REGTRANS-MS` files in `C:\Windows\System32\config\TxR`. These are registry transaction logs, not Windows Search transaction files. That article also addresses a Search service that will not start, not catalog corruption.
findings.quote: Endpoint troubleshooting that removes documented Search transaction files and reboots
findings.suggested_fix: Say "removes registry transaction log files (`.BLF`/`.REGTRANS-MS` under `C:\Windows\System32\config\TxR`) per Microsoft's Search-service-not-starting procedure".

findings.explanation: No cited source documents Search Event 1004 or its meaning. The referenced Q&A shows Event 1008 ("starting up and attempting to remove the old search index {Reason: Index Corruption}") as the corruption-related startup event.
findings.quote: Microsoft-Windows-Search Event ID 1004 indicating startup/rebuild context outside this fault contract
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the Windows Search startup/rebuild event IDs on a supported build. Use a verified ID (likely 1008) in the negative fixture and in the drilldown to "adjacent Search startup/rebuild events", or describe it generically without an ID.

findings.explanation: Service Control Manager's 7040 (service start type changed) is written to the System log, not Application. A real-world collision would therefore come from a different Application provider, and this fixture does not represent an observed case.
findings.quote: Application Event ID 7040 from provider `Service Control Manager`
findings.suggested_fix: Use a fixture from a different Application-log provider reusing 7040/7042. Alternatively, state that the SCM 7040 collision is a System-channel case already excluded by `source=XmlWinEventLog:Application`.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The search embeds `use_case="UC-1.2.88"` as an output column (template residue). It also has no repeat aggregation, although the implementation's notification policy assumes one; see the implementation finding.

summary: A tight, provider-qualified UC whose 7040/7042 semantics match observed Windows Search messages. However, the notification policy in the prose (repeated 7040) is not what the SPL does. One reference is a community post presented as Microsoft Support, and the TxR repair files are mislabelled as Search files.
